checks: Checked a21ff89aef880b49 §§1–2, (4)–(9) against the pinned archive and its declared SHA. Both limit statements and the direct sign inversion match.
Independent centered exponential phases give variance k+p²+1+mb². The mass on either side is k+p, and each magnitude lies in [0,1], giving k+1 ≤ σ² ≤ 2(k+p) ≤ 2(k+1), including b=0 and p=0 or 1.

Use the logarithm analytic at zero. Its tail from degree three has size at most |u|³/(3(1−|u|)) ≤ 2|u|³/3. The sum of cubic coefficient magnitudes is at most σ², so the total fixed-frequency error is bounded by 2|t|³/(3σ), independent of m.
The k unit positive phases give the modulus bound. On [0,σ], k/(4σ²) ≥ k/(8(k+1)) ≥ 1/16. On [σ,∞), the inequality 1+u² ≥ 2u yields exactly 2·2^(−k/2)/k on integrating u^(−1−k/2).

The sign inversion has the positive imaginary-part sign for E exp(itZ). E|Z| ≤ 1 and the Gaussian envelope dominate the zero-extended integral on [0,σ]; the other integral vanishes by the tail estimate. Damped Fubini and both limit passages are justified, with no atom at zero from the independent fixed negative exponential.

Every sequence with k→∞ obeys the same estimates, so failure of uniformity would supply a contradictory sequence. For fixed k, the mean and variance of b_jY_{m_j} give convergence in probability, and coupling plus the no-atom argument treats both p endpoints.
